answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding each identity to a stylometric fingerprint from its public writing. Enrollment takes 30 days of daily work, while a model learns its sentence rhythm and vocabulary. The identity must keep that style for 90 days before earning voting rights. Copying one style across 50 accounts collapses them into one fingerprint, and faking 50 distinct styles costs a human editor about 20 hours each, $1,000 per identity. Like an orchard grafted from different cuttings, each voice stays distinct, and a bridge built from one stolen opal cannot carry a crowd.
